newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi's YANPET mandates banks for $2.322 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Saudi's YANPET mandates banks for $2.322 bln loan.

text.p: Saudi Yanbu Petrochemical Co (YANPET) said on Tuesday it had reached an agreement with a consortium of local, regional and international banks to secure a $2.322 billion loan.
YANPET, owned by Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp and Mobil Corp, said the loan would be used to finance a major expansion project.
"According to the agreement reached on July 22, the consortium has been given the mandate to underwrite and arrange the loan," a YANPET statement said. The consortium consists of 11 banks.

They are Riyad Bank, Arab National Bank, Saudi American Bank, Saudi British Bank, Gulf International Bank, ANZ Banking Group Ltd, Bank of America, Barclays Bank Plc, Chase Investment Bank Ltd, J.P. Morgan Securities Ltd and Sumitomo Bank Ltd.
YANPET in May awarded Fluor Daniel, a unit of Fluor Corp a contract to double its petrochemical complex's capacity in Yanbu on the Red Sea to make it one of the world's largest petrochemical complex.

YANPET said the expansion will add a 800,000 tonnes per year ethylene cracker to the complex and other plants to produce several derivative products such as 535,000 tonnes of polyethylenes, 410,000 tonnes of ethylene glycol, 260,000 tonnes of polypropylene and 125,000 tonnes of pyrolysis gasoline.
The expansion, due to be completed in the year 2000, will double its capacity to around 3.6 million tonnes a year.
